title: Training Note — The Repeat Multiplier for Accounts with Earlier Late Report Penalties
content:
**The rule.** On the Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts, the larger of the flat penalty and the wage share is multiplied by a repeat multiplier before any limit applies:

| Late report penalties booked on the account within its repeat lookback | Repeat multiplier |
|---|---|
| Two or more | 2.0 |
| Exactly one | 1.5 |
| None | Not multiplied |

The repeat lookback is counted in whole months back from the day the penalty is worked out, by the entry dates of the late report penalties in the account's balance history.

## Questions and answers (hypothetical figures)

**The larger of the flat penalty and the wage share is USD 360.00 and one late report penalty lies within the repeat lookback. What amount goes forward to the limit?** 360.00 multiplied by 1.5, that is USD 540.00.

**Same amount, two penalties within the repeat lookback?** 360.00 multiplied by 2.0, that is USD 720.00.

**Same amount, one penalty booked before the repeat lookback begins and none inside it?** It is not multiplied; USD 360.00 goes forward.

**Is the multiplier applied after the limit?** No. The multiplication comes first, and any limit applies to the multiplied amount.
